attack_technique: Endpoint Denial of Service: Service Exhaustion Flood
description: Adversaries may execute 'Low-and-Slow' Application Layer DoS attacks to exhaust server resources. Tools like Slowhttptest simulate attacks such as Slowloris or Slow POST by opening legitimate HTTP connections and deliberately keeping them alive for as long as possible by sending fragmented, incomplete HTTP headers or extremely slow POST message bodies, ultimately exhausting the server's concurrent connection pool.

patterns.description: Extreme anomalies in how long connections are held open and the pacing of the packets within those connections.

features.name: Extreme Connection Longevity
features.description: The overall lifespan of a single network flow (High Flow Duration) is artificially extended for minutes or even hours, as the attacker actively prevents the connection from timing out.

features.name: Prolonged Inter-Arrival Times
features.description: There are massive, deliberate delays between the packets sent by the client (High Flow IAT Mean and High Fwd IAT Max). The attacker waits until the absolute last millisecond before the server's timeout threshold to send the next piece of data.

patterns.description: Anomalies indicating a deliberate lack of bandwidth utilization to fly under the radar of volumetric DDoS protection.

features.name: Minimal Packet Transmission Rate
features.description: Unlike volumetric floods, the number of packets sent per second (Low Flow Pkts/s) is incredibly low. The attack relies on holding connections, not flooding the network.

features.name: Micro-Packet Fragmentation
features.description: The average size of the packets being sent (Low Packet Length Mean) is tiny. The attacker may send HTTP headers or POST bodies just one byte at a time to artificially prolong the transmission.

patterns.description: Specific behaviors within the HTTP protocol used to hold the stateful connections.

features.name: Incomplete HTTP Headers (Slowloris)
features.description: The client continuously sends partial HTTP headers but intentionally never sends the final carriage return/line feed (CRLF) sequence that tells the server the request is complete.

features.name: Slow HTTP POST (R-U-Dead-Yet)
features.description: The client declares a large 'Content-Length' in the HTTP header, but then transmits the actual POST body at an excruciatingly slow rate (e.g., 1 byte every 10 seconds).

patterns.description: Contextual indicators for distinguishing the attack from poor network conditions.

features.name: Volumetric Detection Evasion
features.description: Because the attack uses perfectly valid TCP handshakes and requires almost zero bandwidth, it effortlessly bypasses traditional Layer 3/Layer 4 DDoS mitigation hardware and rate-limiters.

features.name: High-Latency Client Resemblance (False Positive Filtering)
features.description: Legitimate mobile users on extremely poor cellular networks (e.g., edge-of-cell coverage) or clients connecting through high-latency satellite links/proxies can occasionally mimic these slow HTTP behaviors.
